source_name: Nexi Group press-release archive (parent of Nets; SI-relevant processing announcements)
why_relevant: Nexi (having absorbed Nets) is the supplier behind Bankart's instant-payments rails and a pan-European acquirer/POS vendor. Its press-release archive is the canonical feed for any future SI bank or Bankart contract, card-issuing or POS announcement. No SI-specific release was located in this pass.

source_name: Sloexport — Database of Slovenian Exporters (company cards incl. BANKART d.o.o.)
why_relevant: Export-directory company cards describe what SI payments/IT firms actually sell abroad and to whom, which surfaces vendor-side capability and market claims (e.g. Bankart's regional processing) that are otherwise only on marketing pages. Useful as a systematic list of SI banking-technology suppliers to then chase for references.

source_name: NLB Group corporate pages on Bankart (ownership/role disclosure)
why_relevant: Bank-side page describing Bankart's role in processing modern payment instruments for the group and market. Anchors the vendor-route analysis: it establishes the ownership/commercial link that makes Bankart's supplier choices binding on most SI banks' card and ATM estates.

source_name: Finance.si (Časnik Finance) — business daily, banking/finance desk
source_subtype: business daily newspaper / paywalled news site
why_relevant: Slovenia's only business daily; the reference outlet for bank profitability, fee (provizije) changes, card business, market-share disputes and pre-publication leaks of Banka Slovenije / bank figures. Its journalists routinely obtain bank pricelist changes and interchange/fee commentary that never appears in English.

Leading national daily; produced concrete comparative reporting on bank service costs (which banks are cheapest/most expensive), on banks earning the bulk of fee income from basic services, and on ATM network / free-account policy debates. Interprets Banka Slovenije cost comparisons for a general audience.

source_name: Svet kapitala (Delo) — capital markets and finance vertical
why_relevant: Delo's dedicated finance/capital vertical carrying longer-form analysis and commentary on banks, fintech and financial regulation — the closest Slovene equivalent to a specialist finance commentary blog attached to a major title.

Public broadcaster, free and archived; carries the fastest and most complete Slovene-language reporting on instant payments (Flik / verification of payee), Banka Slovenije statements on preserving cash and payment infrastructure, ATM density and consumer studies on basic payment accounts. Often the de-facto public record when STA copy is syndicated.

source_name: STA — Slovenska tiskovna agencija (Slovenian Press Agency)
why_relevant: National wire whose copy is the upstream original behind much of the banking/payments coverage republished by RTVSLO, Delo, Siol, Žurnal24 and regional titles. Tracking STA lets you detect a story at origin and identify which outlets merely mirror it; STA also runs an English service (sta.si/en) useful for cross-checking.

Third major national daily with a business section; historically covers bank consolidation, branch and ATM closures and consumer banking costs. Named explicitly in the cell scope; included as a standing watch even though this run surfaced fewer direct hits than Delo/RTVSLO.

Business magazine published inside the N1 group; produced targeted pieces on neobank cash-withdrawal costs, on what ministers propose for cash/card payments and free basic banking packages, and on card/ATM resilience advice from Banka Slovenije. Good for fee-structure detail and policy signalling.

Regional broadcaster/portal with fast coverage of Banka Slovenije communications and macro-financial statements; useful cross-check on whether a central-bank release was picked up and how it was framed.

High-traffic Telekom Slovenije portal; produced practical, data-carrying pieces on Euronet vs bank ATM fees for foreign cards and on ministerial plans affecting ATM networks. Also aggregates N1 Slovenija content, so it doubles as a mirror for paywalled or short-lived items.

Second-city daily; carried explanatory reporting on why banks are removing ATMs. Regional dailies are the best source on branch/ATM withdrawal at municipality level, a dimension the national statistics do not expose.

Non-profit investigative outlet that has broken payments-relevant stories others would not: the BKS Bank core-system migration failure (duplicated direct debits, wrong statements, Flik/payment errors, Banka Slovenije vs Austrian FMA supervision split) and the Revolut/US-correspondent-bank blacklisting of Slovenia. Highest-value source for operational incident and outage intelligence.

Mass-market tabloid-style portal; useful precisely because it popularises survey findings on how often Slovenes still pay cash and amplifies consumer-facing bank incidents (BKS payment failures). Good early-warning signal for public salience of a payments issue.

Largest commercial broadcaster portal; carried the widely cited framing that cash remains markedly more frequent than cards at Slovenian POS. Broad reach makes it the main channel by which ECB SPACE-type findings enter Slovene public discourse.

Consumer-finance vertical that maintains keyword hubs such as 'dvig gotovine na bankomatu' and 'primerjava bank', and publishes recurring cost comparisons across the ~16 banks and 4 savings banks. Effectively a running, dated record of retail fee levels — a cheap proxy for pricing-history reconstruction.

source_name: Bančni vestnik (Združenje bank Slovenije) — banking journal
why_relevant: The only Slovenian monthly journal for money and banking, published continuously since 1951 by the Bank Association of Slovenia and indexed in EconLit; an annual English international issue appears in November. This is the specialist-commentary layer of the cell: bank executives, BSI staff and academics publish payment-system and card-business analysis here, often with numbers before or beyond the news cycle.

Business portal that reported the concrete ATM-density figure (61.1 ATMs per 100,000 inhabitants vs a proposed statutory minimum of 60) — exactly the kind of quantitative detail extracted from draft legislation that the wire coverage omits.

source_subtype: consumer technology news site (sponsored content likely)
why_relevant: Consumer-tech outlet that systematically reviews Slovenian mobile wallets and payment apps (VALÚ, NLB Pay, DH Denarnik, mBank@Net, Flik integrations). Best single Slovene source for product-level feature and rollout detail on domestic wallets — information no statistical release carries.

Portal that independently covered the BKS Bank payment failures (duplicate payments, Flik, statements, late-interest charges) — a useful second Slovene witness for outage and incident stories, letting you triangulate claims rather than relying on a single outlet.

Regional portal network carrying local-angle payments stories ('Bomo Slovenci še dolgo dvigovali gotovino na bankomatih?'). Regional titles surface ATM/branch closures in specific towns long before any aggregate statistic reflects them.

Long-running Slovene technology community whose threads ('Katera banka?', 'Primerjava spletnih bank') accumulate years of user-reported fee changes, app failures, card-acceptance problems and outage timestamps. Reveals-indirectly: it is often the earliest public trace of a payments incident, hours before media pick-up.

source_name: ZPS — Zveza potrošnikov Slovenije (consumer association) bank-cost calculators and VIP magazine
why_relevant: Independent consumer association that maintains an account-cost comparison calculator and publishes tests that the media then report (e.g. the finding that Slovenian banks give misleading information about the basic payment account). Sits between media commentary and primary evidence: it generates the numbers the press amplifies.

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) — news and publications page
why_relevant: Industry association acting as a pointer hub: announces each Bančni vestnik issue, hosts the industry's position statements on fee regulation and cash access, and is the entity whose statements the press quotes in market-share and fee disputes. Snowballing its news feed yields the actor map of Slovene banking spokespeople.

source_name: Delo tag hub: 'Združenje bank Slovenije' (media tag pages as standing watchlists)
why_relevant: Slovene outlets maintain persistent entity tag pages (Delo /tag/, Siol /kljucne-besede/, Cekin /kljucna-beseda/). These are durable, low-cost pointer feeds for any actor (NLB, OTP, Banka Slovenije, ZBS, Flik) and are the cheapest way to build a longitudinal media file per entity without full-text access.

source_name: Deloitte Central Europe — Digital Banking Maturity (DBM) study hub
why_relevant: Deloitte's flagship recurring mystery-shopper study of retail digital banking; Slovenia is explicitly scored (Slovenian banks classified as 'digital latecomers' in the 2020 edition). Gives comparative SI digital-channel and payment-functionality data no public body publishes.
